Mastering is not a gut feeling. It is applied audio engineering. ✍️

Every track gets treated like a research subject. Before deciding on an EQ move, a compression ratio or a saturation stage, it gets measured, compared and analysed.

That is not academic. It is efficient.

Targeted moves instead of plugin roulette. A background in Systematic Musicology and Media Studies at the University of Hamburg is not a line on a website here — it is the working method.

The result: fewer revisions needed, and a reason behind every decision when you ask.

-14 LUFS is not the number your master has to hit. 📉

▸ Spotify plays tracks back around -14 LUFS integrated by default
▸ A louder master is simply turned down on playback
▸ What stays is the damage: flattened transients, less punch
▸ True peak at or below -1 dBTP keeps lossy encodes from clipping

A metal master should be as loud as the genre needs, not as loud as possible.
